title: Intersection of the I-adic filtration of a finite module vanishes near V(I)
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, $M$ a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $N=\bigcap_{n\ge0}I^nM$. Then for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ with $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$ there is $f\in R$, $f\notin\mathfrak p$, with $N_f=0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], i.e. every element of $N$ is annihilated by some power of $f$. (Part (2) of the source, $N=0$ when $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical, is not stated here.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module, line 12257), part (1); its proof uses Lemma 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-basic) and Lemma 00IP (lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero)
